risk_name: Indirect Prompt Injection via Utility Emails
description: Malicious instructions embedded in automated customer communications or invoices hijack LLM-based support agents to exfiltrate grid data or perform unauthorized account actions.
trigger_conditions: Processing of unvetted external text by LLM-integrated systems
known_mitigations: Human-in-the-loop for sensitive actions;Input sanitization;Instruction-input separation

description: AI-driven credit scoring or demand-response priority models inadvertently penalize low-income households based on historical payment patterns, leading to inequitable service shedding.
trigger_conditions: Model training on socio-economic data without fairness constraints
known_mitigations: Bias mitigation algorithms;Diverse training sets;Fairness auditing

risk_name: Denial of Wallet (DoW) on Cloud AI
description: Attackers flood AI-powered grid analytics endpoints with complex queries, exhausting the utility's cloud budget and causing service outages due to cost-limit triggers.
trigger_conditions: Publicly accessible API endpoints without rate limiting

description: Autonomous AI agents managing microgrid storage and frequency response interact in unpredicted ways, causing resonant oscillations and localized hardware damage.
trigger_conditions: Uncoordinated deployment of independent AI agents on the same feeder
known_mitigations: Formal verification of agent logic;Systemic stress testing

description: Usage of sensitive customer smart meter data (revealing daily habits) for model retraining without proper de-identification, leading to potential PII reconstruction attacks.
trigger_conditions: Data pipeline failure to apply differential privacy or k-anonymity

description: Forecasting models fail as renewable penetration reaches levels outside of historical training distribution (OOD), leading to massive balancing costs.
trigger_conditions: Rapid structural changes in the energy mix (e.g. sudden new wind farm integration)

description: AI-based fault detection introduces processing delays exceeding the 100ms threshold, causing failure to isolate grid faults.
trigger_conditions: Increased network jitter or high CPU load on edge controllers

description: High-performance training/inference cycles consume more energy than the AI saves through grid optimization, violating ESG targets.
trigger_conditions: Inefficient model architecture or frequent full retraining

description: Optimization performance degrades exponentially as the number of connected EVs and batteries increases, leading to market dispatch delays.
trigger_conditions: Registration of new DERs exceeding the model's tested input dimensions

description: Edge-deployed AI models for microgrid stability fail to operate when cloud connectivity is lost due to missing local dependency libraries.
trigger_conditions: WAN outage during microgrid islanding event

description: Independent AI bidding agents learn to coordinate price spikes in wholesale energy markets without explicit human instruction.
trigger_conditions: High frequency trading in markets with low liquidity

description: Rapid shifts in AI architecture (e.g., from CNNs to Transformers) render expensive specialized on-premise hardware investments economically unviable.
trigger_conditions: Announcement of breakthrough model architectures incompatible with current accelerators

description: AI deployment costs spiral due to unforeseen complexity in bridging modern ML pipelines with 40-year-old SCADA protocols.
trigger_conditions: Discovery of data format incompatibilities during late-stage deployment
